hints: Calculate the chord gradient $m_{AE} = \frac{y_E - y_A}{x_E - x_A}$ with $A(2, 1.2679)$ and $E(3, 3)$.
walkthrough:
Calculate the gradient of chord $AE$ using $A(2, 3 - \sqrt{3})$ and $E(3, 3)$:
$$m_{AE} = \frac{3 - (3 - \sqrt{3})}{3 - 2} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{1} = \sqrt{3} \approx 1.73205 \approx 1.7321$$

hints: Examine the limiting behavior of the chord gradients as $x \to 3$.
walkthrough:
Observe the progression of chord gradients approaching point $E(3, 3)$ from the left:
$$m_{AE} \approx 1.7321, \quad m_{BE} = 1.9750, \quad m_{CE} = 1.9975, \quad m_{DE} = 1.9998$$
$$\lim_{x \to 3} \frac{f(x) - f(3)}{x - 3} = 2$$

State the suggested derivative value at $E$:
$$\text{The chord gradients approach } 2, \text{ so the gradient at } E \text{ is } 2.$$
